claim_scope: Direct non-interval scan for sign-changing positive-axis roots; not a certified no-fold theorem.
implementation: Python standard-library binary64; composite Simpson quadrature with 1200 panels; 200 t-subintervals; bisection; centered finite-difference branch slope h=1e-5
observed_conclusion: Exactly one sign-changing positive-axis root was observed for every coarse lambda node from 0.630 through 0.643; none was observed from 0.644 through 0.650. Endpoint refinement shows that branch approaching t=1 with a nonzero negative slope and disappearing when b_ob(lambda)=g(1,lambda) changes sign. No numerical signature of an interior fold was observed.
certification_gap: The scan cannot exclude an arbitrarily narrow unobserved root pair. A binding no-fold result requires interval coverage proving partial_t g<0 on the outer branch region and sign/root exclusion on its complement.
